title: Service Advisor
description:
Service Advisor

Location: Wokingham, Berkshire

Salary: £30,000-£38,000 per annum (dependent on experience)

Hours: Monday-Friday, Full-Time (No Weekends)

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and customer-focused Service Advisor to join our aftersales team in Wokingham. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of a professional dealership that values exceptional customer service and offers a healthy work-life balance with a Monday-Friday schedule.

Key Responsibilities
- Welcome customers and provide a professional, friendly service.
- Book vehicles in for servicing, MOTs, diagnostics, and repairs.
- Prepare accurate estimates and explain work required in a clear, customer-friendly manner.
- Liaise with workshop technicians to monitor repair progress.
- Keep customers updated throughout the service process.
- Obtain authorisation for additional work where required.
- Produce invoices and arrange smooth vehicle handovers.
- Promote additional products and services where appropriate.
- Maintain accurate records using the dealer management system.
- Ensure high levels of customer satisfaction and compliance with company standards.

Candidate Requirements
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor within the automotive industry.
- Excellent communication and customer service skills.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads.
- Ability to work efficiently in a busy aftersales environment.
- Experience using dealer management systems is desirable.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.

Benefits
- Salary of £30,000-£38,000 depending on experience.
- Monday-Friday working pattern with no weekend working.
- Company pension.
- Ongoing manufacturer and professional development training.
- Career progression opportunities.
- Employee discounts.
- Friendly and supportive working environment.

If you are an experienced Service Advisor looking for a Monday-Friday opportunity in Wokingham, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Service Advisor
description:
SERVICE ADVISOR

NEWBURY £30,000 BASIC £36,000 OTE + SERVICE PLAN COMMISSION

A GREAT OPPORTUNITY FOR AN EXPERIENCED SERVICE ADVISOR

Looking for your next Service Advisor role with a strong earning opportunity and additional commission available?

This Newbury opportunity offers a £30,000 basic salary with OTE of around £36,000, plus additional commission for service plans - giving you another opportunity to increase your earnings.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for an experienced Service Advisor to join an established automotive business in Newbury.

You'll be working in a customer-focused Aftersales environment, managing customers throughout the service and repair process while maximising every opportunity to deliver a great customer experience.
- £30,000 basic salary
- £36,000 OTE
- Additional commission on service plans
- Customer-focused Aftersales environment
- Opportunity to increase earnings through additional service-plan commission

THE ROLE
- Manage customers throughout the service and repair journey.
- Book vehicles into the workshop and manage customer requirements.
- Provide clear updates on vehicle progress, additional work and completion times.
- Liaise closely with Technicians and the Workshop team.
- Prepare accurate estimates and invoices where required.
- Identify and maximise appropriate additional sales opportunities, including service plans.
- Maintain excellent levels of customer satisfaction throughout the process.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You'll need
- Previous experience as an Automotive Service Advisor.
- Strong customer service and communication skills.
- Good understanding of Service and Aftersales operations.
- Confident working in a busy, target-driven environment.
- Professional and organised approach.

It would be great if you also have
- Previous main dealership experience.
- Experience working with service plans and additional sales.
- Strong upselling and customer retention skills.
- Experience using automotive dealer management systems.

THE PEMBROOK DIFFERENCE

At Pembrook, we keep things straightforward.

We'll give you an honest overview of the role, package and earning opportunity before putting you forward. If you're interested, we'll support you throughout the process and keep you updated from initial conversation through to interview and offer.

Professional, confidential and straightforward - exactly how recruitment should be.

INTERESTED?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, apply today and a member of the Pembrook team will be in touch for a confidential conversation.

We'll take it from there.

title: Sales Support Administrator
company: M2 Professional Recruitment Services Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic professional to join a leading independent provider of commercial finance solutions to businesses during an exciting period of growth.

title: Customer Safety Administrator
description:
We're looking for two Customer Safety Administrators to join the Customer Safety team and provide essential administrative support across Fire Safety, Asbestos, Lifting and Water Safety.

You'll play a key role in supporting the delivery of Customer Safety programmes, coordinating appointments, managing information, monitoring workstreams and producing accurate reports. You'll work closely with internal teams, contractors, customers and other stakeholders to make sure safety programmes are delivered effectively and on time.

Key responsibilities
- Provide effective administrative support to enable the delivery of Customer Safety programmes across Fire Safety, Asbestos, Lifting and Water Safety.
- Coordinate access appointments for Customer Safety programmes and risk assessments.
- Manage and prioritise customer and colleague contacts relating to Customer and Building Safety, including emails, internal requests and telephone enquiries.
- Review digital workstreams, identifying priorities and escalating issues to the Customer Safety team where required.
- Support annual programmes of work and recommendations arising from risk assessments, including allocating work, raising jobs and purchase orders, and communicating with internal and external customers.
- Produce regular assurance reports to support Customer Safety delivery activities and KPI monitoring.
- Collect, input and maintain accurate information within management systems, working with teams and stakeholders to ensure records are complete and up to date.
- Support mandatory and best-practice compliance requirements across the housing sector.
- Help promote the importance of Customer and Building Safety across the organisation and through customer-facing campaigns.

What we're looking for

We'd love to hear from you if you:
- Have a strong administrative background and can work confidently both independently and as part of a team.
- Have excellent IT skills and practical experience using Microsoft applications and internal management systems.
- Have exceptional interpersonal skills and a proactive, enthusiastic and self-motivated approach.
- Have excellent communication skills and enjoy working collaboratively with a wide range of people.
- Are comfortable working in a rapidly changing environment and managing competing priorities.
- Can work effectively under pressure while maintaining a high standard of accuracy and customer service.
- Have excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
- Are confident handling information, maintaining accurate records and producing reports.
- Take pride in delivering an outstanding service to colleagues and the teams you support.
- Understand the importance of Customer and Building Safety and the role effective administration plays in supporting compliance.

For more information or to apply, please submit your Cv or contact Harvey Baker on

title: Lettings Coordinator
description:
Lettings & Viewings Coordinator

Reed are looking for a Lettings & Viewings Coordinator to deliver high-quality property viewings and tenant check-ins across a residential portfolio. This is a field-based role focused on creating a positive customer experience, maintaining high presentation standards and supporting occupancy through excellent face-to-face engagement.

What We're Looking For
- 2+ years' experience in lettings, property management, block management or a similar property role.
- Excellent communication and customer service skills.
- Full UK Driving Licence and own vehicle.
- Able to work two evenings per week and occasional Saturdays.
- Organised, proactive and customer-focused.

Key Objectives
- Deliver professional property viewings.
- Convert interest into tenant applications.
- Ensure vacant rooms are viewing-ready.
- Conduct smooth tenant move-in check-ins.
- Maintain a strong pipeline of applicants.

Key Responsibilities

Viewings & Property Presentation
- Conduct property viewings across the portfolio.
- Confirm appointments and reduce no-shows.
- Ensure properties are clean, presentable and ready to show.
- Provide accurate information on properties and tenancy terms.
- Answer applicant questions professionally.

Property Preparation
- Set up and move marketing materials between properties.
- Ensure vacant rooms meet presentation standards.
- Report any property issues identified.

Tenant Check-Ins
- Complete in-person move-in check-ins.
- Introduce tenants to the property and house rules.
- Deliver a smooth and welcoming move-in experience.
- Assist with check-outs and inventories when required.

Applicant & Pipeline Management
- Qualify applicants and assess suitability.
- Maintain accurate records within the CRM.
- Follow up viewing attendees and warm leads.
- Re-engage previous enquiries where appropriate.

Administration
- Respond to enquiries and arrange viewings when required.
- Update CRM systems and activity trackers.
- Monitor viewing and check-in performance.
- Support the wider team with reasonable business requests.

Working Pattern
- Field-based role with regular travel between properties.
- On-site position with no remote or hybrid working.
- Full UK Driving Licence and own vehicle required.
- Travel within approximately a 15-mile radius of Reading.
- Minimum of two evenings per week (finishing at 7:30pm).
- Occasional Saturday working (typically 6-8 hours).

What's Not Included in This Role
- Closing deals or making final tenancy decisions.
- Ongoing tenant management after move-in.
- Compliance or onboarding administration.
- Property maintenance coordination.
- Marketing strategy responsibilities.
- Desk-based, remote or hybrid working.

This role is ideal for an experienced property professional who enjoys being out on the road, meeting people and delivering a first-class viewing and move-in experience.

title: Recruitment Account Coordinator
description:
Permanent I Full-time I 5 out of 7 days I On-site

Salary: up to £30,000 per annum + bonus

Have you considered a career in recruitment? You possess drive, ambition, discipline, and structure, but haven't yet had the opportunity to put it all into practice? Come and showcase your potential at Staffline.

The Recruitment Account Opportunity

This is your chance to join the UK's largest recruitment business as a Recruitment Account Coordinator. In this role, you'll be providing temporary workers for our Driving operation in Reading.

To excel in this role, your focus will be on customers, committed to delivering the best service, and a natural problem solver. While experience in on-site recruitment would be beneficial, it's not an essential requirement. If you have transferable skills, we can provide training on all the elements essential for success in this position.

What you'll do as a Recruitment Account Coordinator

This role thrives on pace - helping candidates find the best jobs, solving problems, and enhancing the candidate experience and work environment. It's a wonderfully diverse role that will undoubtedly keep you engaged. Here's a glimpse of what you can expect:
- Meeting client deadlines by fulfilling staffing requirements
- Recruitment, selection, and onboarding of workers
- Accurate data input and validation for weekly payroll
- Handling administrative processes such as absences and change requests
- Ensuring compliance and maintaining secure records for audits
- Providing a positive customer experience and efficiently addressing worker queries

The skills you'll develop as a Recruitment Account Coordinator

Throughout your time at Staffline, you'll receive coaching and challenges that will facilitate skill growth. In this role, you can anticipate enhancing skills related to client and relationship management, hiring and staffing processes, and identifying opportunities for performance improvement - among a range of other areas. At Staffline, we actively encourage progression and personal development, with dedicated progression paths for those who join us.

What we need from you

By now, it should be evident that we're dedicated to your development, fair rewards, and encouraging you to excel in your role at Staffline. To succeed in this position, a few things are required:
- Swift adaptation to changing priorities and effective problem-solving skills
- A customer-centric mindset, prioritizing people above all else
- Ideally, experience within the recruitment industry (though not essential)
- A growth mindset, consistently seeking innovative approaches while fulfilling both client and customer needs
- Strong relationship-building abilities, confidently establishing and maintaining connections with clients and customers
- Most importantly, tenacity, drive, flexibility, and a positive attitude toward delivering excellent service.

Diversity and Inclusion: A Core Focus

At Staffline, we are deeply committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We believe that a diverse team brings different perspectives, ideas, and experiences, enhancing our overall effectiveness and success. We value and celebrate the uniqueness of each individual, and we actively encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

Intrigued? Why not apply now? Or if you need more information, get in touch.

Note: All candidates must demonstrate their Right to Work in the UK. A full UK driver's license is highly desired for this role.

title: Receptionist /Administrator
description: Rosemead Surgery is a friendly supportive practice . We are currently looking for a Receptionist /Administrator You will need to have excellent comminication skills and a passion for helping people, and to be able to stay calm under pressure . Previous experience of working in general practice would be a distinct advantage along with a knowledge of the EMIS Clinical System. Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The duties and responsibilities of the role are varied and can change from time to time with direction of the Assistant Practice Manager or Practice Manager. These will included maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system. Processing requests for appointments , visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate health care professional. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines. JOB SUMMARY: It is the responsibility of each receptionist to assist in the smooth running of the Practice in general, and the reception area in particular, and to project a positive and friendly image to our patients and other professionals who may contact us either in person or via the telephone. To facilitate patients accessing the clinical care provided by the practice. To support the GPs and Nurses in providing that care. To act as first point of contact for anyone accessing the practice. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: To ensure that all visitors and telephone callers to the practice are greeted professionally. To ensure all telephone calls are managed appropriately. To manage the flow of patients arriving at the reception desk, for appointments, prescriptions, or queries. To ensure the clinical staffs receive medical records as requested. To ensure that repeat prescriptions are generated accurately and efficiently, within the 48 hours specified by the practice. KEY TASKS: Reception duties: Greeting and booking in or patients for surgeries and clinics. Dealing with patient enquiries efficiently and courteously. The receiving and recording of telephone messages taking appropriate action. Making appointments on EMIS Clinical System, by processing appointment requests for today, future appointments from patients in person and on the telephone. Ensure eConsults are processed daily and assigned appropriately. Ensure patients are signposted to relevant services, e.g. St Marks Hospital, local pharmacy, Social Prescriber, First Contract Physio etc Ensure all tasks are actioned and completed. Processing prescriptions repeats and filing for collection within 48 hours. Advising patients of relevant charges for private services Receiving specimens from patients ensuring all their details have been recorded whilst following Health & Safety policy. Tidying waiting room after surgery, ensuring premises are kept tidy between visits from the cleaning staff, tidy and sort magazines and leaflets, discarding old and damaged items as necessary. Administration duties: To have a thorough knowledge of all practice policies and procedures To work in accordance with written protocols Provide administrative support for clinical staff. Filing patient records and correspondence when necessary. Opening and distribution or practice post. Registering new patients following the Registration Protocol. Scanning of documents onto the medical system. All scanning should be cleared daily. To send letters to patients as necessary. Changing details on EMIS i.e. Change of address, telephone numbers etc. Other Information: Cover for other Reception team members for sickness and annual leave. Ensuring building security/premises at the end of the day and ensure the building is totally secured, internal lights off and alarm activated. To carry out any other duties agreed between employee and the practice to ensure the smooth running of the practice. Confidentiality: While seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this job description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, the Staff Handbook and the Practice Infection Control Policy, this will include: Using personal security systems with the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Keeping own work areas and general/patient areas free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified. Equality and diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers, and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgemental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/professional development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development. Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload, and resources Participate in audit where appropriate. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. NHS Pension Scheme: The post holder will automatically be enrolled in the NHS Pension Scheme (subject to eligibility checks).

title: Recruitment Administrator
description: Looking for a recruitment role where you can make a real difference? Every vacancy our recruitment team fills supports services across our trust, helping to ensure patients receive great care. This is a busy and varied coordination role where you'll manage vacancies through our recruitment system, Trac, from start to finish. You'll create vacancies, arrange interviews, send offers, coordinate pre-employment checks and support candidates through onboarding, helping to ensure a smooth recruitment process and positive candidate experience. You'll work closely with recruiting managers, candidates and colleagues across the Trust, providing excellent customer service and keeping recruitment activity on track. An important part of the role is resolving issues that could delay a candidate's start date, helping us meet our time-to-hire targets while ensuring NHS recruitment standards are maintained. The role is 30 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with flexibility to work your hours between 8am and 6pm. For your first three months you'll be office-based for induction and training. After this, you'll move to our hybrid working model, spending two days in the office and three days working from home. Please note: This role is not eligible for Skilled Worker visa sponsorship under current UK immigration rules. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK. We're looking for someone with strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills and the ability to manage a busy workload. You'll enjoy problem-solving, removing barriers and helping vacancies progress efficiently. Advertise vacancies accurately and effectively, ensuring roles are progressed within agreed timescales. Liaise with Recruiting Managers, Team Leaders, Finance and Human Resources colleagues to ensure job descriptions, person specifications and all recruitment documentation are complete and processed prior to advertisement. Manage the shortlisting, interview and appointment process from start to finish, including offers of employment, contracts and pre-employment checks, supporting candidates through to their start date. Administer the recruitment and selection process in line with the Trust's Recruitment and Selection Policy, ensuring NHS employment check standards are met while proactively resolving issues that could delay recruitment and onboarding. We're committed to supporting career development and offer a range of learning and development opportunities to help you grow in your role. The must haves for this role: Previous, demonstrable experience working in a fast paced administration/customer service role An understanding of the end-to-end recruitment lifecycle Good communication skills, both written & verbal For further information about the role, please see attached job description and person specification. Your application is your opportunity to demonstrate to us how you meet the requirements of the role. We recognise thatAItools can support accessibility, equity and confidence for applicants.However, its important that examples and responses given in your supporting statement genuinely reflect your own experience and abilities, as these will be explored further during the selection process.AImust not be used to provide misleading or false information during any stage of the application journey. In addition to explaining how you meet the person specification, you must complete your employment history for at least the last five years. Any experience, skills or responsibilities referenced in your supporting statement should be evidenced within your employment history. Applications that do not include sufficient employment history to support the experience claimed may not be shortlisted. Were committed to equal opportunities and welcome applications from all sections of the community. Our commitment to inclusion is reflected in our accreditations: Stonewall Proud Employer, Race Equality Matters Silver Trailblazer, Neurodiversity in Business Corporate Member, Disability Confident Leader, Carer Confident Level 2, and the Armed Forces Covenant Gold Award. Reasonable adjustments will be provided to candidates as needed. We welcome a conversation about flexibility and any other questions you may have. Please dont hesitate to call: Azra Azeezil on azra.azeezil@berkshire.nhs.uk wholl be delighted to help. Please note, if we receive a high number of applications, we may close this role earlier than the advertised closing date, so please submit your application as soon as possible.
